newsitem.title: SYRIA: Assad says Syria wants peace with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Assad says Syria wants peace with Israel.

text.p: President Hafez al-Assad renewed on Tuesday his commitment to making peace with Israel, saying Syria did not wish to go to war with the Jewish state.

"We want peace and if we did not there could not have been a peace process," presidential spokesman Joubran Kourieh quoted Assad as telling 44 visiting Israeli Arab delegates, including members of parliament and opposition Labour and Meretz parties.
"No one likes war...and when they (people) are under occupation they want to end it. War is very ugly and we hope that we will not reach something that is worse than what we have now," Assad said.

Assad also said Damascus would not accept a peace that did not return the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967, to Syria and accused Isareli Prime Minister Benajamin Netanyahu of blocking the peace process.
"We will not surrender, and we will not accept but a just and comprehensive peace," he said.
"Syria did not stop the peace process. The process was moving forward and Netanyahu stopped it and wants to pull it back now," he added.

Sporadic Syrian-Israeli peace talks have failed to resume since the May 1996 election of Netanyahu, who has rejected Syrian demands for return of the Golan. Israel's former Labour government had indicated its willingness to trade at least part of the strategic plateau for peace.
Assad said Syria had the impression that the Labour government ousted by Netanyahu wanted peace and peace talks with it had reached "certain stages...including a commitment to withdraw from Golan".

But Netanyahu had gone back on the progress made in talks with the Labour governments of Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres, he said. "The one who rejects what they did and wants to go back...to the beginning of talks is the one who does not want peace," Assad added.

Saleh Tarif, a Labour party member of the Israeli parliament, said he was carrying a call from party leader Ehud Barak to the Syrian leadership for coordinating peace efforts. He did not give details.
The delegation arrived in Damascus on Assad's invitation via Egypt on Friday in the second such a visit to Damascus in 50 years.
The delegates, including writers and journalists, said they came to show support for Syria's demand for the return of the Golan and to improve cooperation with Syria.
Ibrahim Nemer Hussein, head of the delegation and member of the Israeli parliament, said they discussed with Assad ways of holding an Arab summit about Netanyahu's policies.
